sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼等众多嘉宾。

sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日于 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选访谈，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hello, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: My name is Reginald Dwayne Betts.
sentences.zh: 我叫雷吉纳德·德韦恩·贝茨。

sentences.en: And a few years ago, I wrote a piece for the New York Times Magazine about my life.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我为《纽约时报杂志》写过一篇关于我生活的文章。

sentences.en: It was, you know, about going to prison at 16 and coming home, and then my attempts at becoming an attorney.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那是关于我 16 岁入狱、重返社会，以及后来尝试成为一名律师的经历。

sentences.en: And all of it has come back to me more recently and reminded me what the piece was really about.
sentences.zh: 最近这一切又重新涌上心头，让我想起了那篇文章真正的主题。

sentences.en: I was listening to my oldest son, Makai, talk to his classmates, and I heard him say,
sentences.zh: 当时我听着我的大儿子马凯和同学交谈，听到他说：

sentences.en: Hey, as you all know, my father went to jail.
sentences.zh: 嘿，如你们所知，我父亲曾入狱。

sentences.en: And the class, they were talking about the death of George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 当时全班正在讨论乔治·弗洛伊德之死。

sentences.en: And what my son was asking was why prison was the place for a 16-year-old me,
sentences.zh: 我儿子问的是，为什么监狱会是 16 岁的我的归宿，

sentences.en: and why prison would have been the place had Floyd gotten arrested and convicted of passing a fake $20 bill.
sentences.zh: 如果弗洛伊德因使用一张假 20 美元钞票被捕并定罪，为什么监狱也会是他的归宿。

sentences.en: Prison would have been the place for him.
sentences.zh: 监狱本会是他的归宿。

sentences.en: And why that same place would be the place for, if convicted, the officer that killed Floyd.
sentences.zh: 为什么如果那个杀害弗洛伊德的警官被定罪，同一个地方也会是他的归宿。

sentences.en: And I think what he was asking is just, what is punishment in America?
sentences.zh: 我想他问的其实是：美国的惩罚到底是什么？

sentences.en: What is it for, and how should we think about it?
sentences.zh: 它的目的是什么，我们又该如何看待它？

sentences.en: And the part about it all that encouraged me, I think, is that listening to my son, I could hear that he wasn't ashamed of what I did.
sentences.zh: 而这一切中最让我感到欣慰的是，听着我儿子的声音，我能听出他并没有为我做过的事感到羞耻。

sentences.en: He recognized it was wrong.
sentences.zh: 他认识到那是错误的。

sentences.en: But the hurt really came from knowing that he lives in a society that imagined prison was the place for me.
sentences.zh: 但真正的痛苦来自于意识到他生活在一个认为监狱是我的归宿的社会里。

sentences.en: And maybe from living in a society that imagines prison is the place for anybody.
sentences.zh: 也许也来自于生活在一个认为监狱是任何人的归宿的社会里。

sentences.en: So here's my piece, Getting Out, read by J.D.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我的文章《出狱》，由 J.D.

sentences.en: Jackson.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊朗读。

sentences.en: One afternoon, in the fall of 2016,
sentences.zh: 2016 年秋天的一个下午，

sentences.en: I sat in a windowless visiting room at the Manson Youth Institution in Cheshire, Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 我坐在康涅狄格州柴郡曼森青年收容所一间没有窗户的会客室里。

sentences.en: A recent graduate of Yale Law School,
sentences.zh: 作为耶鲁法学院的新近毕业生，

sentences.en: I was a certified legal intern on a fellowship in the New Haven Public Defender's Office.
sentences.zh: 我是纽黑文公设辩护人办公室的一名带薪实习执业法律实习生。

sentences.en: Jay, a lanky 18-year-old brown-skinned kid sitting across from me, was my first client.
sentences.zh: 坐在我对面的是杰伊，一个身材高瘦、皮肤黝黑的 18 岁男孩，他是我的第一个客户。

sentences.en: He didn't talk.
sentences.zh: 他一言不发。

sentences.en: Instead, he stared at me as if I were the police.
sentences.zh: 相反，他盯着我，就像我是警察一样。

sentences.en: Sanford O.
sentences.zh: 桑福德·奥·

sentences.en: Bruce III, my supervising attorney, listened as I explained to Jay, one of his initials, what we knew of the charges against him.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯三世，我的主管律师，在一旁听着我向杰伊——用他名字的一个缩写——解释我们所了解到的对他的指控。

sentences.en: A young man with whom Jay attended high school had claimed that Jay and another kid he didn't know had threatened him with a pistol
sentences.zh: 一个与杰伊上同一所高中的年轻人声称，杰伊和另一个他不认识的男孩用手枪威胁他，

sentences.en: and then robbed him of his cell phone and a couple of hundred dollars.
sentences.zh: 然后抢走了他的手机和几百美元。

sentences.en: Officers arrested Jay minutes later, but the other suspect, who supposedly held the gun, was never found.
sentences.zh: 警察几分钟后就逮捕了杰伊，但那个据称拿着枪的嫌疑人却一直没有找到。

sentences.en: The prosecutor thought he should serve time in prison.
sentences.zh: 检察官认为他应该在监狱里服刑。

sentences.en: I let Jay know this and described what would happen next.
sentences.zh: 我把这一点告诉了杰伊，并描述了接下来会发生的事情。

sentences.en: A series of court dates, a bond reduction motion, plea bargain offers.
sentences.zh: 一连串的庭审日期、保释金减免动议、认罪协商的提议。

sentences.en: After remaining silent for nearly 40 minutes, he leaned forward in the blue plastic chair, cutting me off, and asked, aren't you the one who did time in prison?
sentences.zh: 在沉默了近 40 分钟后，他前倾身体靠在蓝色塑料椅上，打断了我，问：你不是那个坐过牢的人吗？

sentences.en: With a single question, this kid reminded me of what a law degree, even one from Yale, could not do.
sentences.zh: 仅仅用了一个问题，这个男孩就让我回想起了一个法学院学位（哪怕是耶鲁的学位）所无法做到的一点。

sentences.en: Make my own criminal history vanish.
sentences.zh: 抹去我自己的犯罪前科。

sentences.en: On December 7th, 1996, a month and two days after my 16th birthday,
sentences.zh: 1996 年 12 月 7 日，在我 16 岁生日一个月零两天后，

sentences.en: I climbed with four other people into a beat-up, ink-colored sedan in Prince George's County, Maryland.
sentences.zh: 我和另外四个人一起挤进了一辆马里兰州乔治王子县破旧的墨色轿车里。

sentences.en: During that year,
sentences.zh: 那一年，

sentences.en: I'd read the Evelyn Wood Guide to Speed Reading and J.
sentences.zh: 我读过《伊夫林·伍德快速阅读指南》和 J.

sentences.en: California Cooper's novel,
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚·库珀的小说，

sentences.en: The Wake of the Wind.
sentences.zh: 《风的踪迹》。

sentences.en: My advanced-placement U.S.
sentences.zh: 我在苏特兰高中的高级美国

sentences.en: history teacher at Suitland High School had nicknamed me Smokey after he spied me rolling a blunt before his first period class.
sentences.zh: 历史老师给我取了个外号叫“斯莫基”，因为他在第一节课前瞥见我在卷大麻烟。

sentences.en: I hadn't won a fight since second grade, had been suspended half a dozen times.
sentences.zh: 自从二年级以来我就没打过架，但已经被停学过六次。

sentences.en: Once for setting off a stink bomb, but every other time for what teachers called being disruptive, but was really just talking too much.
sentences.zh: 其中一次是因为引爆了臭气弹，但其他所有时候都是因为老师所说的“具有破坏性”，其实不过就是话太多。

sentences.en: People knew me for finding four-leaf clovers, doing backflips, and making too many jokes.
sentences.zh: 人们都知道我喜欢找四叶草、翻后空翻以及开太多玩笑。

sentences.en: I didn't know who I was.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己是谁。

sentences.en: The driver, who was in his early 20s, was a stranger to me.
sentences.zh: 司机二十出头，对我很陌生。

sentences.en: I half knew his cousin.
sentences.zh: 我只勉强认识他的表弟。

sentences.en: I'd brought my friend Marcus, who had played on the junior varsity basketball team with me, to the cousin's house to get high.
sentences.zh: 我把曾和我一起打过校二队篮球的朋友马库斯带到了他表弟家去嗨大麻。

sentences.en: In the passenger seat, another face I'd just met said a robbery would pad our pockets.
sentences.zh: 在副驾驶座上，另一张我刚认识的面孔说抢劫能让我们的口袋鼓起来。

sentences.en: Weed, ignorance, and a desire for a come-up, wanting just a few more dollars than we had, made us believe him.
sentences.zh: 大麻、无知、对发财的渴望，以及想要比现有更多一点钱的念头，让我们相信了他的话。

sentences.en: We ended up on I-95 at night, headed to the Springfield Mall in Fairfax County, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我们在夜里上了 95 号州际公路，前往弗吉尼亚州费尔法克斯县的斯普林菲尔德购物中心。

sentences.en: The driver gave me his pistol, because I'd asked for it.
sentences.zh: 司机把他的手枪给了我，因为我向他索要了。

sentences.en: I stared at it, my life about to be riven.
sentences.zh: 我盯着它，意识到我的人生即将支离破碎。

sentences.en: He told me not to take the gun safety off for any reason.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我在任何情况下都不要打开枪支保险。

sentences.en: An accidental gunshot could get us all killed or sent to prison for life.
sentences.zh: 一次走火就可能让我们全部送命或者被判终身监禁。

sentences.en: At the mall, I first approached two people headed toward a parked car.
sentences.zh: 在购物中心，我首先走向了两个正朝一辆停放的汽车走去的人。

sentences.en: My arms stretched toward the ground, the pistol dangling in my hand.
sentences.zh: 我的双臂伸向地面，手枪在我手中晃荡。

sentences.en: One of them turned and saw me.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人转过身看到了我。

sentences.en: Before I knew it, two women jumped in their car and disappeared.
sentences.zh: 还没等我反应过来，两个女人就跳进车里消失了。

sentences.en: Minutes later, I approached one of the few cars in the lot.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，我走近停车场里为数不多的几辆车之一。

sentences.en: I saw a man asleep.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个男人在睡觉。

sentences.en: I tapped twice on the window with the pistol's barrel, demanded that he get out of the car and turn over his keys and his wallet.
sentences.zh: 我用枪管敲了两下车窗，要求他下车并交出车钥匙和钱包。

sentences.en: Marcus and I drove away in the stolen vehicle.
sentences.zh: 马库斯和我开着偷来的车逃走了。

sentences.en: The next day, before the end of the Sunday church service
sentences.zh: 第二天，在周日礼拜结束之前，

sentences.en: Marcus's mother attended, the police had us in handcuffs, caught at a different Virginia mall shopping with another man's credit card.
sentences.zh: 也就是马库斯的母亲参加的那场礼拜，警察就给我们戴上了手铐——我们在弗吉尼亚州的另一个购物中心用别人的信用卡购物时被抓获了。

sentences.en: After meeting with Jane,
sentences.zh: 在与杰伊见面后，

sentences.en: I sat in my office with his file.
sentences.zh: 我拿着他的档案坐在我的办公室里。

sentences.en: A thin sheaf of no more than a dozen pages.
sentences.zh: 一叠薄薄的档案，不过十几页。

sentences.en: I pulled out my own criminal record.
sentences.zh: 我拉出了我自己的犯罪记录。

sentences.en: One hundred odd pages spilled from the accordion folder.
sentences.zh: 厚厚的一百多页从风琴夹里倾泻而出。

sentences.en: I stared at the documents scattered across my desk.
sentences.zh: 我盯着散落在办公桌上的文件。

sentences.en: My neat cursive on the handwritten confession.
sentences.zh: 我那份手写供词上整齐的草书。

sentences.en: A faded yellow summons demanding my mother appear in court as if my crime belonged to her.
sentences.zh: 一张泛黄的传票，要求我母亲出庭，仿佛我的罪行属于她一样。

sentences.en: The sentencing order consigning me to prison.
sentences.zh: 将我送进监狱的判决令。

sentences.en: The prison scrubs that Jay wore.
sentences.zh: 杰伊穿的囚服。

sentences.en: The jail cell that held him.
sentences.zh: 关押他的牢房。

sentences.en: The early mornings when deputies would take him shackled and cuffed to court.
sentences.zh: 副警长们带着戴着脚镣手铐的他去法庭的那些清晨。

sentences.en: Connected us.
sentences.zh: 将我们连接在了一起。

sentences.en: I wanted him to believe that the worst of what might happen could be overcome.
sentences.zh: 我希望他相信最糟糕的事情是可以克服的。

sentences.en: But I wasn't sure if that was true.
sentences.zh: 但我并不确定这是真的。

sentences.en: Some ten months later,
sentences.zh: 大约十个月后，

sentences.en: I would receive a letter from the Connecticut Bar Examining Committee.
sentences.zh: 我将收到一封来自康涅狄格州律师考试委员会的信。

sentences.en: The committee, it said, would not recommend me for admission to the bar.
sentences.zh: 信中说，委员会不会推荐我获得律师资格。

sentences.en: Under Connecticut law, felons are presumed to lack the character and fitness required to practice law unless they can prove otherwise.
sentences.zh: 根据康涅狄格州法律，除非重罪犯能证明自己具备资格，否则将被推定为缺乏执业所需的品格和适格性。

sentences.en: I might eventually be allowed to practice law or, I realized with a cold, dull clarity,
sentences.zh: 我最终也许会被允许执业，或者——我带着一种冰冷、麻木的清醒意识到——

sentences.en: I might not.
sentences.zh: 我也许不会。

sentences.en: One time in prison,
sentences.zh: 在监狱里的某一次，

sentences.en: I watched a man crack the jaw of another man with a padlock rolled up in a sock.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个人用一块包在袜子里的挂锁砸裂了另一个人的下巴。

sentences.en: Everyone knew the victim as the man who made wine by letting bread, fruit, and jelly ferment in a black trash bag.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道受害者是个会把面包、水果和果冻放在黑色垃圾袋里发酵来酿酒的人。

sentences.en: He brought happiness and escape to the men there.
sentences.zh: 他给那里的男人们带来了快乐和解脱。

sentences.en: When he was struck, blood squirted from his nose and mouth.
sentences.zh: 当他遭到袭击时，鲜血从他的鼻子和嘴里喷涌而出。

sentences.en: He seemed startled that such pain had found him, astonished that he had been hurt in that way.
sentences.zh: 他似乎对这种痛苦会找上自己感到震惊，对以那种方式受到伤害感到错愕。

sentences.en: But me?
sentences.zh: 但我呢？

sentences.en: I'd known what to expect before the disappointing news from the bar examiners arrived.
sentences.zh: 在收到来自律考官令人失望的消息之前，我就已经知道会发生什么了。

sentences.en: And still,
sentences.zh: 即便如此，

sentences.en: the latter left me weeping.
sentences.zh: 后者还是让我泪流满面。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Months after pleading guilty to carjacking, attempted robbery, and a firearm charge,
sentences.zh: 在对劫车、企图抢劫和持枪指控认罪几个月后，

sentences.en: I sat shackled and cuffed in the Fairfax County courthouse, waiting for my sentencing.
sentences.zh: 我戴着脚镣手铐坐在费尔法克斯县法院里，等待宣判。

sentences.en: I faced a maximum of life plus 13 years.
sentences.zh: 我面临着最高终身监禁外加 13 年的刑期。

sentences.en: My mother, two aunts, and one uncle, along with two family friends, sat in the audience, anxious,
sentences.zh: 我的母亲、两个阿姨、一个叔叔以及两个家庭朋友坐在旁听席上，忧心忡忡，

sentences.en: the man whose car I'd stolen quietly looked on.
sentences.zh: 我偷了车的那个男人静静地注视着。

sentences.en: Back then, I would have said we hadn't injured him, but the truth is that PTSD is a real injury, and the pistol I waved in his face may stay with him still.
sentences.zh: 当年，我会说我们没有伤害他，但事实是创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）是一种真正的伤害，我在他脸前挥舞的手枪可能至今仍留在他的记忆中。

sentences.en: My mother didn't testify.
sentences.zh: 我母亲没有作证。

sentences.en: Bronchitis had taken her voice, but I knew heartbreak had left her unable to speak my name without crying.
sentences.zh: 支气管炎夺去了她的声音，但我知道是心碎让她无法在不哭泣的情况下说出我的名字。

sentences.en: I couldn't forget how devastated she looked when I told her what I'd done.
sentences.zh: 我无法忘记当我告诉她我做了什么时她看起来是多么绝望。

sentences.en: Three witnesses, my Aunt Pandora and the two family friends, spoke on my behalf.
sentences.zh: 三位证人——我的阿姨潘多拉和两位家庭朋友——为我进行了求情发言。

sentences.en: Their testimony was punctuated with the talk that troubles courtrooms where young black men are sentenced to prison.
sentences.zh: 他们的证词中穿插着那种让判处年轻黑人男性入狱的法庭感到困扰的谈话。

sentences.en: He was having difficulties making that adjustment of not having a father in the household.
sentences.zh: 他一直在努力适应家里没有父亲的状况。

sentences.en: Before sentencing me,
sentences.zh: 在对我进行宣判之前，

sentences.en: Judge F.
sentences.zh: 法官 F.

sentences.en: Bruce Bach asked if I wanted to address the court.

sentences.en: Maybe we all pursued law to save someone left behind.
sentences.zh: 也许我们所有人追求法律都是为了拯救被抛在身后的人。

sentences.en: Maybe we pursued it to save ourselves.
sentences.zh: 也许我们追求它是为了拯救我们自己。

sentences.en: Prison taught me how to wait.
sentences.zh: 监狱教会了我如何等待。

sentences.en: I learned to break up a nine-year sentence into a million moments of waiting.
sentences.zh: 我学会了把九年的刑期拆解成数百万个等待的瞬间。

sentences.en: Waiting for rec, for chow, for count time, waiting for mail call, for visits, waiting to walk in the world without thinking constantly about danger, waiting for freedom.
sentences.zh: 等待放风，等待开饭，等待点名，等待送信，等待探视，等待走在世界上而不用时刻想着危险，等待自由。

sentences.en: Waiting to hear back from the bar committee felt similar.
sentences.zh: 等待律师协会委员会的回信也有类似的感觉。

sentences.en: Once again, I was just waiting for mail.
sentences.zh: 又一次，我只是在等信。

sentences.en: When the letter came, it began,
sentences.zh: 当信件到来时，开头写着：

sentences.en: Dear Mr. Betts, the Connecticut Bar Examining Committee is pleased to advise you that you have been recommended for admission to the Connecticut Bar on November 3rd, 2017,
sentences.zh: “亲爱的贝茨先生，康涅狄格州律师考试委员会很高兴地通知您，您已被推荐于2017年11月3日获得康涅狄格州律师资格，

sentences.en: two days before my 37th birthday.
sentences.zh: 在我37岁生日的两天前。”

sentences.en: My mother, along with my Aunt Pandora and Uncle Darren, who had driven more than 300 miles to watch it all, walked into the New Haven Superior Court on 235 Church Street.
sentences.zh: 我的母亲，以及潘多拉阿姨和达伦叔叔——他们驱车300多英里来观看这一切——走进了位于教堂街235号纽黑文高级法院。

sentences.en: They deposited keys, watches, belts, and cell phones into a gray bucket before walking through a metal detector.
sentences.zh: 他们在穿过金属探测器之前，将钥匙、手表、皮带和手机存放在一个灰色的桶里。

sentences.en: Minutes later,
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，

sentences.en: Therese Mackay Miles and I followed them through the same gauntlet.
sentences.zh: 特雷斯·麦凯·迈尔斯和我跟着他们穿过了同样的关卡。

sentences.en: Most black families walking into this courthouse are headed into a disaster.
sentences.zh: 大多数走入这座法院的黑人家庭都是走向一场灾难。

sentences.en: But that day, my folks joined my friends and colleagues in a small fourth floor courtroom to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 但那天，我的亲人们和我的朋友、同事一起聚集在四楼的一个小法庭里进行庆祝。

sentences.en: Inside, the deep, rich mahogany pews called to mind the Fairfax County courtroom where I learned I'd do time.
sentences.zh: 在里面，深色而华丽的桃花心木长椅让我想起了我得知自己要入狱的费尔法克斯县法庭。

sentences.en: Looking around,
sentences.zh: 环顾四周，

sentences.en: I thought about the squalor and violence of the prison cells.
sentences.zh: 我想起了牢房的肮脏和暴力。

sentences.en: Minutes later, I stood before Judge Omar Williams with my friend and supervising attorney,
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，我站在奥马尔·威廉姆斯法官面前，身旁是我的朋友兼主管律师

sentences.en: Sanford O.
sentences.zh: 桑福德·O·

sentences.en: Bruce III, who goes by Trey.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯三世，大家都叫他特雷。

sentences.en: The swearing in, for most, is simply a ritual.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，宣誓就职只是一种仪式。

sentences.en: In courtrooms across the country, judges administer the oath to countless new attorneys each time bar results are released.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地的法庭上，每当律师考试结果公布时，法官都会为无数新律师主持宣誓。

sentences.en: But this was different.
sentences.zh: 但这不一样。

sentences.en: I stood alone before the judge with just a lawyer to the right of me, as I'd done so many years before.
sentences.zh: 我独自一人站在法官面前，右边只有一个律师，就像我多年前做的那样。

sentences.en: Trey asked the court to approve my admission to the Connecticut bar.
sentences.zh: 特雷请求法庭批准我加入康涅狄格州律师协会。

sentences.en: You fought long and hard with the sword to get here today,
sentences.zh: “你为了今天能来到这里，曾手持长剑历经长久而艰难的斗争，”

sentences.en: And today,
sentences.zh: “而今天，

sentences.en: you're presented with the shield.
sentences.zh: 你获颁了盾牌。”

sentences.zh: 就在那天的近三年前，作为耶鲁大学法学院二年级学生，

sentences.en: I walked into the office that Trey and Judge Williams, then a public defender, shared.
sentences.zh: 我走进了特雷和当时身为公设辩护人的威廉姆斯法官共用的办公室。

sentences.en: I told Trey that I had a record and asked if it would be a problem for me to work in the criminal justice clinic.
sentences.zh: 我告诉特雷我有案底，并询问这是否会成为我在刑事司法诊所工作的障碍。

sentences.en: He told me that if there was anyone who should be working in the clinic, it was someone like me, who from experience understood what the clinic's clients were going through.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，如果说有谁应该在诊所工作，那就是像我这样的人，他通过经验理解诊所客户所经历的事情。

sentences.en: Reciting the oath to become a member of the court took a fraction of the time that it took me to be sentenced.
sentences.zh: 背诵成为法庭成员的誓言所花费的时间，只占我被判刑所花时间的一小部分。

sentences.en: I wondered if becoming an attorney would fill the hole in my mother's heart that my becoming a felon created.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，成为一名律师能否填补我母亲心中的那个空洞——那个因为我成为重罪犯而造成的空洞。

sentences.en: The courtroom was where she lost her son.
sentences.zh: 法庭曾是她失去儿子的地方。

sentences.en: Maybe it would be where she got him back, too.
sentences.zh: 也许这里也是她找回儿子的地方。

sentences.en: I could see my mother wiping her eyes, but smiling this time.
sentences.zh: 我能看到母亲在擦拭眼睛，但这次她在微笑。

sentences.en: Someone clapped.
sentences.zh: 有人鼓掌。

sentences.zh: 我的达伦叔叔拿出手机在录像。

sentences.zh: 特雷斯，早在这一切成为可能之前就已经陪伴在那里的人，

sentences.zh: 正满面春风。

sentences.zh: 她的双臂环抱着

sentences.zh: 在那里的每个人都知道我曾经走出法庭走向监狱，除了我的小儿子

sentences.zh: 迈尔斯，他才六岁。

sentences.en: Therese and I hadn't decided when we would let Miles know, but we hoped that it would be on our terms, and not because of a classmate or an overheard conversation.
sentences.zh: 特雷斯和我还没有决定什么时候让迈尔斯知道，但我们希望这是按我们的意愿，而不是因为某个同学或偶然听到的对话。

sentences.en: After the 15-minute ceremony,
sentences.zh: 15分钟的仪式结束后，

sentences.en: I turned to everyone without thinking, and began speaking as my uncle kept recording.
sentences.zh: 我没有多想便转向大家，在叔叔持续录像的同时开始讲话。

sentences.en: The last time my mom saw me in court,
sentences.zh: 妈妈最后一次在法庭上看到我时，

sentences.en: I was sentenced to nine years in prison.
sentences.zh: 我被判处了九年监禁。

sentences.en: I wanted to say something about the journey.
sentences.zh: 我想对这段旅程说点什么。

sentences.en: I'd already revealed too much.
sentences.zh: 我已经透露得太多了。

sentences.en: Miles, sitting beside his brother,
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯坐在他兄弟旁边，

sentences.en: paused and looked up.
sentences.zh: 停顿了一下，抬起头来。

sentences.en: I could tell something confused him.
sentences.zh: 我看得出有什么东西让他感到困惑。

sentences.en: He had questions in his eyes.
sentences.zh: 他的眼中带着疑问。

sentences.en: He stared, listening, as I confessed the thing that I'd been holding back.
sentences.zh: 他盯着我，听着我倾诉我一直隐瞒的事情。

sentences.en: What man wants to tell his child he's done time in prison?
sentences.zh: 哪个父亲愿意告诉自己的孩子他坐过牢？

sentences.en: But I had.
sentences.zh: 但我确实说了。

sentences.en: And in that single breath,
sentences.zh: 就在那一呼一吸之间，

sentences.en: I'd given him this,
sentences.zh: 我给了他这个——

sentences.en: an image of his father as both a convict and an attorney.
